No. For 26 September to 26 October 2026, FIRMS recorded zero thermal detections intersecting asset ASSET-F07.

This result is well supported. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, VIIRS NOAA-20, VIIRS NOAA-21 and MODIS) have status "covered" for the full period, which meets the run's rule that every day be covered by each sensor. The spatial test was whether a detection footprint intersects the asset.

Two caveats:
- The asset's area is not recorded (null), so I can't comment on its size. Small fires on a small property could fall below the sensors' resolution.
- The data is near real time, so later quality processing could change it slightly.

A zero count means FIRMS detected no active fire or thermal anomaly there. It does not prove that no burning occurred.
